dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi there! I'm looking for a good book to buy. I'm hoping to find something within a reasonable budget — preferably under $15. I'd love something in the comic or mystery genre. Do you have anything like that?
dialogue.agent:

A few standouts: **"Web of Deceit"** is free, has an excellent 4.3 rating with 238 reviews, and is described as a "comic murder mystery" — seems like it might check both your boxes! **"Thrilling Mystery"** is also well-rated at a low price.

products.title: Thrilling Mystery - 05/38: Adventure House Presents:
Web of Deceit (The Dewey Webb Historical Mystery Series Book 1)
products.description: About the Author Renée Pawlish is the award-winning author of the bestselling Reed Ferguson mystery series, the Dewey Webb mystery series, horror bestseller Nephilim Genesis of Evil, The Noah Winters YA Adventure series, middle-grade historical novel This War We're In, Take Five, a short story collection, and The Sallie House: Exposing the Beast Within, a nonfiction account of a haunted house investigation. Renée has been called "a promising new voice to the comic murder mystery genre" and "a powerful storyteller". Nephilim Genesis of Evil has been compared to Stephen King and Frank Peretti. Renée was born in California, but has lived most of her life in Colorado. --This text refers to an out of print or unavailable edition of this title.

products.title: Up in the Air
The Paris Enigma: A Novel
products.description: Review “Luminous...a tightly spun thriller...Mr. De Santis effortlessly incorporates important historical events (the building of the tower and the World’s Fair) into his narrative, as well as capturing the turn-of-the-century uneasiness over the emergence of the machine age.” — Wall Street Journal “[An] outstanding puzzler. . . . De Santis adroitly explores such issues as the difference between image and reality while providing intelligent and entertaining discussions of alternate approaches to detection.” — Publishers Weekly (starred review) “[A] beguiling historical whodunit . .. .” — New York Times Book Review From the Back Cover In the tradition of The Alienist and The Devil in the White City comes a gripping, atmospheric tale of murder and the art of crime solving. Paris, 1889: in anticipation of the World's Fair and the opening of Monsieur Eiffel's tower, a society of the world's most famous detectives convenes as a single body for the very first time. Sent in place of a conspicuously absent Renato Craig, founding member of The Twelve, his novice assistant Sigmundo Salvatrio arrives, bearing a secret message for the brilliant, brooding Viktor Arzaky, Craig's best friend and the society's cofounder. When one of The Twelve is discovered murdered at the Tower's base—the first in a series of grisly slayings—it falls to Arzaky and Salvatrio, the last remaining student of Craig's famed Academy for Detectives in Buenos Aires, to find and stop the killer. But what the two discover as they race around fin-de-siècle Paris—encountering secret societies, philosophical puzzles, and an imperiled, dangerously beautiful woman—has shattering consequences that will alter the fate of their precious brotherhood forever. About the Author A journalist and comic-strip creator who became editorin chief of one of Argentina’s leading comics magazines,Pablo De Santis is the author of six critically acclaimed novels, one work of nonfiction, and a number of books for young adults. His works have been published in more than twenty countries. He lives in Buenos Aires. Read more

products.title: Nancy Drew and the Clue Crew #2: Secret Sand Sleuths
products.description: From Booklist Nancy, Bess, and George are back for another adventure as the elementary-school students join their class in a field trip to a local museum. The mystery is no less flimsy in the second volume of the Nancy Drew and the Clue Crew series, but it does take up more of the plot. The nice addition of a Buddhist monk who is working on a sand painting offers some calm amid the chaos of the hyperactive kids. The cheerful art and the name-brand tie-in will draw young readers looking for hard-to-find mystery graphic novels. Grades 2-5. --Snow Wildsmith About the Author Sarah Kinney has written over 150 original Disney comics for Egmont Publishing, and co-wrote the Nancy Drew and Nancy Drew: The New Case Files #1 and #2 for Papercutz with Stefan Petrucha. Her non-comics work includes the animated feature Blaze of Glory for Santoon Pictures. Stefan Petrucha has written X-Files comics and for Disney Comics. He is the author of such YA series as Timetripper , Split , The Rule of Won , and Blood Prophecy , which was published in 2010 to rave reviews. Stefan authored the hit Papercutz graphic novel "Tales From the Crypt #8: Diary of a Stinky Dead Kid" and appeared on the most reason season of A&E's Paranormal State . Stan Goldberg started his comics career in 1949 at age 16 as a staff colorist for Timely Comics, now known as Marvel Comics. Stan designed the colors of some of the most popular characters of the 1960's, including Spider-Man , The Fantastic Four , The X-Men , and The Hulk . He has had an extremely prolific career that stretches across 5 decades. In the 1990's he gained notoriety for drawing the Riverdale characters for the wildly popular Archie Meets the Punisher crossover between Archie and Marvel. He works as an artist for Archie Comics to this day.

result.title: A is for Apocalypse: An ABC book on the many horrific and awful ways the world ends.
result.features: Awaken your inner doomsday prepper with a laugh. During the ‘unprecedented’ times of our lives it’s always good to remember that things could be worse. Much worse. A is for Apocalypse humorously delves into the dark expanse of our thoughts and fears with easy to understand cartoons and captions. What will doomsday look like? Well, it looks like an ABC book. Whether with a giant Earth busting asteroid or microscopic nanobots eating everything, you can be sure that there’s a letter and illustration associated with the end of days. This book lies somewhere in the nether between the humor of Go the F**k to Sleep and All My Friends Are Dead. It’s a book with a horribly deranged and comical take on Apocalyptic scenarios. You might say it’s not your average alphabet book.

result.title: Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)
result.features: Amanda Warren's Next Murder...Amanda and Jace are spending a blissful week in North Carolina when her daughter Katie calls-- she's being held for questioning in the murder of popular TV finance guru Kevin Patterson. They rush back to New Jersey, where Amanda meets Jace's beautiful ex-NYPD partner, Lori Malone, the detective who's holding Katie for questioning. This case is out of Jace's jurisdiction but he and Amanda must find the killer to clear Katie's name. The stakes rise quickly as they unearth Patterson's connection to a powerful international drug cartel. Can Amanda and Jace find the killer-- and clear Katie's name-- before someone kills them first?

top_reviews.title: Loved it. Hilarious.
top_reviews.text: Saw this on a whim and thought it looked funny. Way better then I could have asked for. Super funny, though i may wait to share with my nephews.

dialogue.agent:
Here's what the reviews say for both books:

**1. "A is for Apocalypse"** — $4.57 | ⭐ 5.0
The one review says: *"Loved it. Hilarious. Saw this on a whim and thought it looked funny. Way better than I could have asked for. Super funny, though I may wait to share with my nephews."* It's a humorous cartoon ABC book about apocalyptic scenarios — dark comedy with illustrations. If you enjoy funny, offbeat humor, it could be a fun, cheap pick!

**2. "Blood Orange Death (An Amanda Warren Mystery)"** — $12.99 | ⭐ 5.0
The reviewer says: *"Amanda Warren grows on you. She's very human, and somehow vulnerable as she forges a new life after a bitter divorce... Grab yourself a Blood Orange dessert, and get in on the fun and romance as Amanda works her magic on another Jersey Shore mystery. You'll love it!"* So it's a proper murder mystery with a strong lead character, some romance, and a suspenseful plot.

So to summarize:
- **"A is for Apocalypse"** — A comic/humorous ABC book with dark humor and cartoons. Great if you want something light and funny.
- **"Blood Orange Death"** — A traditional mystery novel involving a daughter suspected of murder and a drug cartel. Great if you want a gripping whodunit.

Which sounds more like what you're after?

top_reviews.title: What could be worse than having your own daughter held under suspicion of ...
top_reviews.text:
What could be worse than having your own daughter held under suspicion of murder? Not trusting the cop you love to keep an objective viewpoint when an old flame turns up, that's what!

Amanda Warren grows on you. She's very human, and somehow vulnerable as she forges a new life for herself after a bitter divorce. Everything would be great, in fact, except for the unsolved murders that keep cropping up around her. Grab yourself a Blood Orange dessert, and get in on the fun and romance as Amanda works her magic on another Jersey Shore mystery. You'll love it!

dialogue.user:
Thanks for the details! Honestly, both sound like they have good qualities, but I'm not fully convinced that either of them is quite right for me. 

"A is for Apocalypse" sounds fun and is a great price, but it's more of a humor/comic ABC book rather than a proper comic story or a mystery — it doesn't really scratch both the comic AND mystery itches I have.

"Blood Orange Death" does sound like a solid mystery, but it doesn't seem to have any comic elements to it.

I was really hoping to find a book that fits both my interests — comic and mystery — while also having that 5.0 rating and staying under $15. Do you have any other options, or have we covered everything? I'm not quite feeling confident enough to buy yet.
dialogue.agent:
I've searched thoroughly, and unfortunately, there are no books under $15 that combine both comic and mystery elements with a perfect 5.0 rating. That's a very specific combination, and our inventory just doesn't have one that matches all three criteria at once.

Here's what I can offer though:

- **"A is for Apocalypse"** ($4.57, 5.0 ⭐) — dark humor with comics/cartoons, albeit not a narrative comic story
- **"Blood Orange Death"** ($12.99, 5.0 ⭐) — a solid mystery but no comic elements
- **"Web of Deceit"** ($0.00, 4.3 ⭐ with 238 reviews) — the closest hybrid, actually described as a "comic murder mystery," though it falls slightly short on rating

If a 5.0 is firm, **"A is for Apocalypse"** at $4.57 or **"Blood Orange Death"** at $12.99 are your only options. If you'd be willing to consider the 4.3-rated **"Web of Deceit"** — it's free, has a ton of reviews, and truly is a comic murder mystery — it might be your best fit overall.

Otherwise, I'm afraid we've covered everything available. Would you like to go with one of these, or would you rather pass?

dialogue.user:
Thank you for being so thorough! I appreciate all the effort you put into finding options for me. Unfortunately, the 5.0 average rating is really important to me, and I was hoping for something that truly blends comic and mystery elements. None of the available books quite hit all my criteria perfectly. I think I'll have to pass on this for now.

Thanks again for your help!
